What am I looking at?

The spectrum separates sound into frequency components using the browser’s FFT analyzer. Frequency runs logarithmically from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, or the input’s Nyquist limit. Each display band shows its strongest FFT bin. Thin caps hold recent peaks. The waveform below shows amplitude over time; the waterfall stacks the latest 64 spectra into a moving landscape.

A sine wave has one main frequency. Square and sawtooth waves add harmonics; triangle harmonics fade more quickly. Use the frequency slider while the test tone is playing to move these peaks. Larger FFT sizes distinguish nearby frequencies more clearly, over a longer time window. Smoothing averages successive spectra.

The signal level is RMS in dBFS, relative to digital full scale, not calibrated sound pressure. Strongest frequency is an estimate of the largest spectral peak, not necessarily the musical fundamental. Microphone response and browser processing affect measurements.

Audio is processed locally: there is no recording or upload. Microphone access starts only when you choose it and approve the browser prompt; microphone audio is never played through the speakers. Stop audio, leaving the page, or switching tabs releases the microphone and stops playback. Freeze view freezes only the picture. With reduced motion the view starts frozen; choose Resume view for continuous analysis.

Audio files use codecs supported by your browser. Web Audio reference ↗
